titleEn: I'm Sorry—Let's Fold It Together Again!

pages.text: "Only Sonu's boat floats well!" Mina, a handspan taller than Sonu, peered into the yard tub. The round-bellied youngest child's leaf boat floated happily. Low river water meant they had fetched only a little today.
"I want one that floats, too." Mina set their boat down again, but it overturned. A finger pressed Sonu's boat down, sinking it.
"My boat!" Sonu looked into the tub, near tears. Mina grew hot to the ear tips. 'I should say sorry...' But the words stuck in their throat.
Mina sat at the platform's edge, back turned. Alone, Sonu fished out wet leaves. Tap, tap. The yard grew quiet.
Mom came from hanging laundry and sat beside Mina. "Something seems caught in your throat." Mina only looked at their toes.
Then Sonu toddled over with the wet leaf. "It won't float now." Mina braced hands on the platform and straightened up.
Mina took a big breath in and out. "I pushed it down. I'm sorry. Shall we fold it together again?"
The stuck feeling slipped away. Sonu smiled and held Mina's hand. "Yes! Together!"
They floated the leaf boats they had folded together. "Mine floats now, too!" Mina smiled. Two boats floated side by side.
Mom hugged each child with one arm. Mina leaned on Sonu. "This time, both boats go together."
